subject: Food Science
title: Flavor Encapsulation
description: Learn Flavor Encapsulation in one minute.

hook.text: Scratch-and-sniff stickers work because aroma molecules are trapped inside microscopic capsules that burst when scratched.

buildup.text: Flavor encapsulation wraps volatile compounds in protective shells—starches, gums, or proteins.

discovery.text: Spray drying is the most common method: liquid flavor is atomized into hot air with a carrier matrix, forming powder particles.

twist.text: Chewing gum flavor fades because encapsulated flavors release in controlled bursts.

climax.text: Timed-release capsules can deliver flavor sequentially—first sweet, then sour, then mint.

punchline.text: Flavor Encapsulation: the goal is not certainty, but sharper thinking.

quiz.question: Why does chewing gum flavor eventually fade?
options: Encapsulated flavor capsules are all broken—the base gum has no inherent flavor
